sources.name: ODOT SAFE-T (Statewide Analysis for Engineering & Technology; OU ITS Lab hosts it)
sources.access: gated (personal account, eligibility tied to employment; private-sector users sign a Permit)
sources.gps_share: not measured ('Not all crashes found are mappable')
sources.keys_linkable: Collision ID; each unit and person has its own ID, exported with the Collision ID (SAFE-T Training pp. 112-113)

sources.name: OCERS (Oklahoma Collision Electronic Records System, DPS / OHSO)
sources.access: gated (agency login; single reports by request)
sources.years: about 2023 on (official record; rollout to all agencies ongoing)

sources.name: OHSO public KAB layers (kab_crashes_2019, 2020_kab_crashes, 2021_kab_crashes)
sources.years: 2019-2021, fatal + serious + minor injury crashes only

sources.name: OHSO SORTPO_OCERS (Southern Oklahoma RTPO region, 16 counties)
ODOT AllCollisions_2012_2021
sources.years: 2012-2021, I-35 corridor only (39,688 of 39,752 rows on I-35)

blockers: SAFE-T accounts are for 'government agencies for transportation safety related activities' and 'may not be used for private projects' (SAFE-T Training p. 5)
the open statewide layers are fatal/serious/minor-injury only and stop in 2021
no published SAFE-T or OCERS export column list (SAFE-T has a 'User Data Dictionary' behind the login)
user_actions: Ask ODOT Traffic Analysis (ODOT-CollisionData@odot.org) whether a private firm may hold a SAFE-T account and use exports inside a paid tool, or ask for a statewide 2020-2024 extract
Alternatively ask OHSO (405-523-1570) for a statewide OCERS extract, 2023 on, all severities
Send Engineering one SAFE-T 'Export Collisions' CSV (one county, one year, all fields) and its User Data Dictionary to confirm ok-column-map.json
